title: Saints Peter and Paul (29 June)
hook: the fisherman and the tentmaker, the two pillars of Rome

segments.voice: Yesterday, the birth of John the Baptist and a father who wrote a name, Yohanan. Your line was his name is john. Whose name did you ask about? Day six hundred seventy-five.

Two giant stone statues stand guard in front of Saint Peter's Basilica in Rome. On one side, Peter, holding keys. On the other, Paul, holding a sword. The Church gives them one feast together, on the twenty-ninth of June. Which is a little funny, because they didn't always get along. One was a fisherman from Galilee. The other was an educated Pharisee from a city in what is now southern Turkey who made tents for a living. And once, in front of everyone, one of them told the other he was wrong.
screen: `KEYS AND A SWORD.` → `THE FISHERMAN AND THE TENTMAKER.` → `ONE FEAST FOR BOTH.`

segments.voice: Peter first. Simon, son of John, a fisherman, renamed by Jesus, in the Douay-Rheims: "thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church." Petros, rock. The keys in his statue come from the next line, the keys of the kingdom. Catholics see in Peter the first of the popes, the bishop of Rome. He's also the one who sank in the water, who denied Jesus three times, and who was forgiven on a beach. Then Paul. Saul of Tarsus, who persecuted the first Christians until a light knocked him to the ground. Acts says he worked as a tentmaker, and in his letters he says he worked night and day while he preached, so as not to be a burden. Now the argument. In his letter to the Galatians, Paul tells how Peter came to Antioch and ate with Gentile Christians, then pulled back when some men came from James in Jerusalem. Paul writes: "I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed." The Church kept that letter in the Bible. Both men ended up in Rome, and tradition says both died there under the emperor Nero. Peter, the story goes, was crucified, and asked to be crucified upside down. Paul, a Roman citizen, was beheaded, which is why he holds a sword. In the second letter to Timothy, Paul says: "I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith." Two pillars, the Church calls them. Different, sometimes at odds, holding up the same roof.
screen: `PETROS: THE ROCK, AND THE KEYS.` · `SAUL THE TENTMAKER.` · `I WITHSTOOD HIM TO THE FACE.` · `TRADITION: BOTH DIE IN ROME.` · then, large: `I HAVE FINISHED MY COURSE, I HAVE KEPT THE FAITH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold the Church of Rome. Sit, and picture the city: the basilica over Peter's grave, the pope, the parishes, the people on buses and the poor sleeping near the colonnade. If you pray, you can pray for the pope and for the people of Rome. If you don't, think of two people in your own life who don't always agree, but hold something up together, and be grateful for both. The bell holds the time.
Petros. The Greek word for rock, the name Jesus gave Simon just before the keys of the kingdom. Today's word.
Your line: two pillars. Today, thank someone you've disagreed with for the thing you hold up together: a family, a team, a parish. Day six hundred seventy-five.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the solemnity of Saints Peter and Paul on 29 June; in Rome it's a city holiday, and the pope blesses the pallium, a woolen band, for archbishops appointed during the year.

trapdoor: what you thought: two saints who always agreed.
what it means: a fisherman and a tentmaker, sometimes at odds, both martyred in Rome, kept on one day.
what a scholar hears: Galatians 2's clash at Antioch; tradition, not scripture, gives Peter's upside-down cross and Paul's beheading under Nero.

notes: Upside-down crucifixion of Peter comes from the apocryphal Acts of Peter, via Origen/Eusebius; framed as tradition.
Paul's beheading as a Roman citizen: tradition; confirm.
Pallium blessing for new metropolitan archbishops on 29 June; confirm current practice.
Galatians 2:12 'stricter visitors' summarizes 'certain came from James'; confirm fair framing (not a foil for Jewish practice).

Editor review (2026-10-01): hook no longer opens 'Walk into'; invented 'smelled of the lake' cut; Matthew 16:18 quote starts at the Douay's own words ('thou art Peter', the verse reads 'That thou art Peter'); 'so as not to be a burden' moved from Acts to Paul's letters (1 Thess 2:9); Galatians 2:12 now says 'men came from James' instead of 'stricter visitors'; 'in the 60s' cut; 2 Timothy named instead of 'Paul's own words near the end'.
